correctness.rationale: For each j, the exact density follows from Catalan counts of paths with j-1 births and j deaths and 2j-1 independent exponential holding times. Given count and total duration, jump order and normalized holding times have a parameter-independent uniform Catalan/Dirichlet kernel, proving full-path equivalence. A generalized ballot convolution gives the joint sufficient-statistic law, hence the exact NP risk series. Conditional L-1 sign changes prove strict total-variation improvements against either marginal. Expectations of N-1 and T give the exact KL formula and conditional-Gamma gap; score variance gives Fisher information. An iid score CLT and Taylor expansion yield local testing error; monotonic KL yields the sharp expected covert-insertion constant. Critical finite identities were checked by 125 passing standalone numerical/integer tests (see verification_output.txt); neither unbounded summation nor limit assertions rely on finite experiments.

These are explicitly credited, not claimed new. Compared with those stronger premises, the specific new claimed joint-monitoring outcome is the exact finite NP error series, strict detection-power separation from both marginal reports for all k, the closed information gain and the sharp covert queueing constant, none stated in the inspected relevant primary documents. Residual priority risk remains for earlier specialised inferential work not inspected in full.

value.rationale: A newly studied covert queueing model exposes either count or duration, naturally raising what changes when both are revealed. The exact full-path-equivalence theorem is a structural optimal-data-compression result for arrival-rate inference. Its strict all-finite-sample TV improvement quantifies the privacy consequence of the pair, and its explicit optimal-error series and KL covert constant give actionable mathematical quantities without requiring observers to see individual jumps. It is not a gratuitous fixed-parameter calculation or a mere renaming of the classical busy-period distribution.
